light.definition: Green / yellow / red lights, one per output, from signals the model has at run time. * duct present? how undecided the probability is, p(1 - p) * duct strength spread of the ensemble members' predictions (M-units) * duct thickness spread of the ensemble members' predictions (m) For each signal, green is at or below the validation-year median, red is above its 85th percentile, yellow is between. The cut-offs are fixed on the validation year before the test period is looked at. The overall light is the worst of the three. Red means: do not rely on this estimate, rerun the full simulation. Why three lights and not one: a confident "strong duct" has a large strength spread but a very certain presence, while a coin-flip presence usually means a weak or absent duct whose strength error is small. One shared score ranked the errors in opposite directions, so each output gets the signal that actually tracks its own error.
